requirements.title: A substring is a parent string followed by an explicit parenthesized substring range
requirements.definition: The syntactic form of a substring is exactly parent-string followed by parentheses containing a substring-range. The substring-range is not optional: a whole scalar character variable, scalar character component, array element, coindexed named object, or character constant without the following range is not a substring under R908.

The non-vacuous contrast is that the whole variable remains a valid designator but not a substring form.

requirements.title: Parent strings are the five scalar character-capable designator or constant forms
requirements.definition: A parent-string is one of five alternatives: scalar-variable-name, array-element, coindexed-named-object, scalar-structure-component, or scalar-constant. Array sections, whole array names, non-scalar structure components, arbitrary expressions, function references not otherwise a scalar constant, and parenthesized character expressions are not additional R909 alternatives.

requirements.title: A substring range is a colon with optional scalar integer endpoints
requirements.definition: A substring-range consists of an optional first scalar-int-expr, a required colon, and an optional second scalar-int-expr. Both endpoints may appear, either endpoint may be omitted, or both may be omitted, but the colon is always present and any endpoint expression is scalar integer.

requirements.title: The parent string of a substring is character typed
requirements.definition: For every R909 parent-string alternative used in a substring, the parent-string shall be of type character. The constraint is on the parent string, not on the endpoint expressions or on the value selected by the substring.

requirements.title: Substring value, defaults and length follow the effective starting and ending points
requirements.definition: A substring is a contiguous portion of a character string. The first scalar-int-expr supplies the starting point f and the second supplies the ending point l; omitted f defaults to 1 and omitted l defaults to the parent string length n. Parent characters are numbered from 1 through n, and the substring contains the characters from f through l inclusive in sequence. Its length is MAX(l - f + 1, 0), so f greater than l yields a zero-length substring.

requirements.title: Nonzero substrings require effective endpoints within the parent string numbering
requirements.definition: When the effective starting point is not greater than the effective ending point, both endpoints shall be within the range 1 through n, where n is the parent string length. The stated range condition is not applied by this sentence to the zero-length case where the starting point is greater than the ending point. Endpoint values can be compile-time constants or execution-time expression values, so any future diagnostic plan must distinguish static numbered constraints from this unnumbered prose restriction.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_088.json reads all eight original 9.4.1 units and their28 fine units in full, verifies the census hashes and all502 grammar heads, and confirms that R908-R910 require an explicit substring-range, so a whole scalar variable or array element is not a substring occurrence. C908 keeps its character-type condition on the parent string. The starting and ending points, the MAX(l-f+1,0) length, the default endpoints of one and n, the zero-length case when the starting point exceeds the ending point, and the requirement that both endpoints otherwise lie within one through n remain distinct conditions, with runtime-valued endpoint conditions not given an invented static diagnostic duty. The illustrative note stays informative. All36 facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
